key_claims: Alzheimer's disease progresses as a continuous biological process.
Most existing neuroimaging-based AI methods are limited to discrete diagnosis or clinical score prediction from cross-sectional imaging.
The proposed Disease Continuum Positioning (DCP) framework continuously estimates disease severity from longitudinal diffusion tensor imaging (DTI).
DCP models disease severity as a low-dimensional probabilistic latent variable by integrating longitudinal observations with weak clinical supervision.
The Disease Continuum Score (DCS) quantifies an individual's position along the Alzheimer's disease continuum with associated uncertainty.
Experiments on the ADNI cohort show DCP consistently outperforms representative disease progression methods.
limitations: The source is an abstract and does not provide detailed methodology or full results.
The specific performance metrics and statistical significance are not reported.
The generalizability to other cohorts or clinical settings is not addressed.
The source does not discuss potential limitations or biases of the approach.
what_not_to_say: DCP is a causal model for Alzheimer's disease.
DCS is a validated clinical biomarker.
DCP has been approved for clinical use.
The study includes specific numerical results or effect sizes.
The framework is superior to all other methods in all settings.
